title: BlueCrest POC scoping - workload modeling
next_steps: Redwood to send POC scope + pricing by 2026-03-04
BlueCrest to share 2 weeks of anonymized traffic logs by 2026-03-06
Schedule benchmark run window (30-60 min) week of 2026-03-09
action_items: Alex Chen: Draft POC scope and pricing (due 2026-03-04)
Maya Li: Export and anonymize last 2 weeks of inference traffic (due 2026-03-06)

summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling to size a 4-week pilot for BlueCrest Payments. Discussed QPS, concurrency, input/output token distributions, success criteria (latency, cost per 1k requests, quality thresholds), and benchmark plan. Action items and timeline agreed.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro: I'm Alex Chen, AE at Redwood. With me is Samir, our SE, and Priya on solutions.
[00:12] Maya (BlueCrest): Hi, Maya here, eng lead at BlueCrest. Tom on in a minute.
[00:18] Tom (BlueCrest): Tom Reynolds, CTO. Sorry for joining slightly late.
[00:24] Samir (Redwood SE): No worries. Goal for today is to nail down POC scope around workload modeling — QPS, concurrency, token distributions, and what success looks like.
[00:35] Nina (BlueCrest Product): We want to validate latency and cost tradeoffs before committing to a dedicated pool.
[00:40] Alex: Perfect. Maya, can you describe the current traffic shape? QPS peaks, typical concurrency, input sizes?
[00:48] Maya: Sure. Our live inference is used for payment risk scoring and some fraud chat features. Peak QPS is around 220 requests per second for the scoring API during peak hours, sustained peaks maybe 10-15 minutes. Baseline daytime QPS is 40-60. Concurrency on our app tier is around 180-200 concurrent requests, but at the inference layer we see bursts of 250 concurrent connections sometimes.
[01:12] Rafael (SRE): To add, the scoring requests are very short — avg input tokens about 12-25 tokens, outputs are small, like 10-30 tokens. The chat flow has bigger messages, avg input ~180 tokens, output ~150 tokens but chat is only ~8% of total traffic.
[01:32] Samir: That's helpful. So main workload is low-token scoring with high QPS, and a smaller chat workload with longer sequences. For sizing we usually model both independently and then aggregate.
[01:44] Tom: Our primary success criteria are 99th percentile latency under 200 ms for scoring, cost per 1k calls below $X (we gave a ballpark in the RFP), and no degradation in model quality vs baseline. We also need audit logs and SSO readiness.
[02:01] Alex: Understood. For the POC we propose: 2-week pilot (3 weeks if needed) with benchmark runs: synthetic replay of anonymized traffic + live canary at low volume. We'll measure p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost telemetry, and regression on a small eval set.
[02:17] Maya: Sounds good. A few clarifying q's: 1) Do you support VPC peering for private deployment during pilot? 2) Can you simulate our boundary conditions where bursts hit 250 QPS?
[02:28] Priya: Yes to both — for Redwood Private we can set up VPC peering or Secure Connect; for hosted we do region-based routing but we can also spin a dedicated customer pool for the POC if you prefer. We can replay your logs to simulate peaks including 250 QPS bursts.
[02:43] Nina: How about KV cache behavior and batching? In our scoring flow we often have repeated prefixes, so we want to measure cache hit impact.
[02:52] Samir: Great point. Our runtime supports prefix/KV caching and continuous batching. For the replay we can enable prefix cache and run experiments with cache enabled/disabled to quantify gains. Note: transcript sometimes shows "k v cash" in auto transcription – apologies for any typos.
[03:08] Maya: We're also evaluating quantized models vs full fp16; cost differences are material. Can you run both?
[03:15] Samir: Absolutely. We'll run the same model in fp16 and int8/4-bit quantized variants where possible. We'll capture output quality deltas on your eval prompts.
[03:24] Tom: For the scoring model, we currently run an in-house distilled LLM with a avg latency of ~120 ms on our infra but cost is high. We're interested in Redwood's managed option if we can meet latency and reduce cost by at least 25%.
[03:37] Alex: Noted. We'll include comparative cost modeling. For the POC benchmark configuration we need: anonymized request logs (timestamps, input token counts, output token counts), a small eval prompt set for quality checks, and any infra constraints for VPC/peering.
[03:51] Rafael: We can provide logs as a gzipped csv, we'll scrub PII. Timeline: we can export and hand over by EOD 2026-03-06.
[03:58] Alex: Great. On our side Samir will prepare the replay harness and benchmark scripts. Priya will draft the POC scope and pricing.
[04:07] Maya: How do you model concurrency vs QPS? Our concern is that QPS peaks don't translate linearly into required GPU count because of short tokens.
[04:16] Samir: Right. We model both. Key inputs: requests per second distribution, request size distribution (input tokens), output tokens, sequence length distribution, and allowable latency SLO. The runtime simulates effective tokens/sec and effective batch sizes to estimate occupancy. For short requests with small outputs the per-request overhead dominates, so we size for p99 tail — you'll likely benefit from batching only up to a point.
[04:37] Samir: Example we gave in the doc: a 200 QPS workload with avg 20 in / 20 out tokens maps to X tokens/sec; on A100-class we might sustain Y rps with Z latency. We'll produce concrete numbers for your traces.
[04:52] Nina: What's the plan for canarying? We want to run a low-volume live canary to validate end-to-end.
[04:58] Priya: Standard approach: replay synthetic traffic against Redwood cluster; then a 1% live traffic canary for 48 hours with full observability. If everything is green we ramp to 10% for 24 hours. We capture p50/p95/p99, error rates, and quality regression.
[05:15] Maya: One more ask: we have strict SOC2 and ISO requirements, plus KMS managed keys. Will audit logs and KMS integration be available during the POC?
[05:23] Alex: Yes, we can enable KMS integration and send a copy of our SOC2 summary and security docs. For POC we can provide an audit log stream or temporary access. We'll attach the security pack to the scope doc.
[05:33] Tom: About benchmarking metrics — we want cost per 1k calls at p50 and p99 latency buckets, and daily cost extrapolate across a month with your autoscaling.
[05:44] Samir: We'll include cost curves: cost vs latency tradeoff, with configurations for batching, quantization, and dedicated vs shared pools. We'll also show routing policy impact.
[05:53] Rafael: On the infra side, network egress during heavy runs may be a constraint. Who handles egress charges in dedicated vs hosted pilot?
[06:01] Alex: We'll outline egress responsibilities in the POC SOW. Typically hosted pilots include egress up to a reasonable cap; dedicated/private will follow customer cloud billing. We'll clarify in the doc.
[06:12] Maya: Ok, timeline review?
[06:15] Alex: BlueCrest provides logs by 2026-03-06. Redwood delivers POC scope and pricing by 2026-03-04. Benchmark harness and initial config delivered by 2026-03-06. Benchmark window scheduled week of 2026-03-09. Pilot starts 2026-03-10 and runs 2 weeks with potential extra week.
[06:34] Nina: That aligns.
[06:36] Samir: On success criteria — let's capture them succinctly: 1) p99 latency for scoring API <= 200 ms, 2) cost reduction >= 25% vs current, 3) quality regression within tolerance (<2% on your eval metrics), 4) ability to sustain 250 QPS bursts without error spikes.
[06:53] Maya: Agree. Also we need SSO/SAML and audit logs working for sign-off.
[06:58] Alex: We'll list those as gating items. Any competitor constraints?
[07:02] Tom: We're running a parallel eval with Anthropic on shorter timeline, and considering OpenAI's managed endpoints for fallback. We want Redwood to demonstrate clear unit-economics and perf.
[07:12] Priya: Understand. We'll include comparative numbers where possible and make the benchmark apples-to-apples.
[07:18] Rafael: Minor note, our logs sometimes have missing output token counts — we can approximate if needed but will try to include them.
[07:25] Alex: That's fine. For the replay harness we can sample and infer output sizes from response bodies if necessary, but prefer explicit counts.
[07:33] Nina: Ok, final recap and next steps please.
[07:36] Alex: Recap: Redwood to send POC SOW + pricing (Alex/Priya) by 2026-03-04; BlueCrest to share anonymized logs and eval prompts by 2026-03-06; Redwood to prepare benchmark harness (Samir) by 2026-03-06; schedule benchmark week of 2026-03-09. Success criteria captured. Security docs and KMS options to be attached.
[07:54] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[07:56] Tom: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:58] Alex: Thanks, bye.

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., "k v cash" for KV cache, mis-attribution). References: shared deck (link: https://redwood.app/decks/bluecrest-poc), security pack (link: https://redwood.app/security-pack), sample benchmark spreadsheet to follow.
